text: Since then, all new hawkers are required to pay rental at market rate.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Hence, there are no subsidised rents in all our new centres.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Last year, I announced the formation of a Hawker Centre 3.0 Committee to review and make recommendations to improve the management of hawker centres and ensure the sustainability of the hawker trade to benefit Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Following a year of extensive consultations with many stakeholders, including hawkers, patrons, cleaning service providers and members of the public, the Committee submitted the recommendations to the Minister in February this year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will, therefore, work together with relevant stakeholders to implement them.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, one key recommendation is for the Government to provide training opportunities and pathways for aspiring hawkers − young or the not-so-young.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For a start, we are working with the People's Association to develop a "Hawker Fare" series of culinary classes, starting in May.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Members of the public can learn how to cook hawker dishes, like chicken rice, yong tau foo and mee goreng from the veteran hawkers themselves.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: While not all trainees will eventually become hawkers, such courses will also help to generate interest in hawker food and culture among Singaporeans and contribute to sustaining the hawker trade in the long run.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There are a handful of culinary certification courses in the market today.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, these courses are largely not tailored for the hawker trade.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Hence, in addition to the Hawker Fare series that focuses on culinary skills, we are working with ITE to develop a separate short course to teach aspiring hawkers relevant business management skills, like basic profit and loss analysis and how to tender for a stall, to help them set up and manage a hawker business.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: More details will be released later in the year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We welcome other interested parties, such as training providers, to work with us to provide appropriate training to aspiring hawkers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In the second half of this year, we will set up a one-stop information and service centre, which will provide useful information to both existing and aspiring hawkers, like how to tender for a stall, where to go for courses on food hygiene and the hawker trade, and the range of kitchen automation equipment available.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This will allow them to decide if they are cut out for the trade without putting in heavy investments.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: (In Mandarin):   The Committee's second recommendation focuses on improving productivity of the hawker centres.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Committee recommended that the Government implement productivity measures in the hawker centres to help hawkers reduce their workload and address the manpower challenges that hawkers are facing.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, productivity initiatives, such as centralised dishwashing and cashless payment, are already a requirement in the new hawker centres.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Some stallholders in existing centres have also voluntarily subscribed to centralised dishwashing services, such as those at Boon Lay Place Market and Food Centre.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This will include some funding to increase the adoption of centre-level productivity initiatives, like centralised dishwashing and stall-level productivity initiatives like the purchase of kitchen automation equipment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This will help lower the initial cost of adoption of productivity measures that will help realise manpower and cost savings in the long term.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Hawkers can start applying for this grant in the third quarter of this year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Some hawkers are already using kitchen automation equipment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When I visited Smith Street Food Centre recently, I came across a cooked food stallholder who sells steamed yam cakes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: She uses an automated stirrer to mix ingredients which reduces a lot of manual labour.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Through the Hawkers' Productivity Grant, we hope to encourage a greater adoption of such labour-saving equipment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Third, more than just dining spaces, hawker centres are places where Singaporeans of all walks of life can interact.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In response to the Committee's recommendation to encourage regular organised activities at hawker centres in a sustainable manner, I am happy to announce that we will be providing funding support of $2,000 per event to adopters of hawker centres, up to an annual cap of $10,000 for each adopter, to organise events to enhance the vibrancy of hawker centres.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Such events can enhance patrons' dining experience at hawker centres, while increasing footfall and benefiting hawkers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Fourth, on graciousness in hawker centres, people recognise that the act of tray-return is a kind and considerate behaviour to be cultivated.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To Mr Png Eng Huat's question, we introduced tray-return to hawker centres in 2012 and, since 2015, tray-return facilities have been implemented in all hawker centres.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The tray-return rates vary, with the highest tray-return rates at Tiong Bahru Market, Blk 157 Tampines Street 11 and Our Tampines Hub.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have also been working on making tray-return stations more visible, prominent and accessible, as seen in the newer hawker centres.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To study how to further improve tray return rates, we are also currently running a pilot involving the use of specially designed tray decals and working with our cleaning contractor at Zion Riverside Food Centre to train the cleaners to encourage patrons to clear their trays after their meals.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These initiatives that we are rolling out are part of our efforts to ensure the sustainability and viability of the hawker trade.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They should help to support both existing and aspiring hawkers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This, in turn, will allow Singaporeans to continue enjoying affordable food in a clean and hygienic environment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Lastly, let me give an update on our dengue cases.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Despite earlier concerns that warmer weather would contribute to a spike in dengue cases to beyond 30,000 last year, we managed to bring the situation under control.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There were instead 13,000 dengue cases last year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The World Health Organization has also commended our efforts in managing the Zika outbreak.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, we cannot be complacent and should remain vigilant by doing the five-step Mozzie Wipeout.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked for an update on the small-scale field studies of Wolbachia-Aedes mosquitoes that commenced last year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: About half of the Aedes aegypti eggs collected from a trial site were unable to hatch.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Our panel of international experts recently affirmed the good progress and expressed their support for NEA's plan to move to the next phase of the suppression trial later this year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To achieve the vision of a liveable and sustainable Singapore, as laid out in our Sustainable Singapore Blueprint, everyone needs to be part of the solution.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The little things that we do, like throwing away our trash properly, recycling our waste responsibly and returning our trays with the crockery properly, can make a big difference.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With the support of this House, Singaporeans can rise up and do this together.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have a bit of time for clarification.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: This is a question for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: With regard to the Pneumatic Waste Conveyance System (PWCS), will it be rolled out to existing HDB estates as well, the older estates, the ones with a lot of bin chutes?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The plan now is to roll it out to the new HDB estates because, to put in the infrastructure, greenfield, will be much easier and more cost-effective to do.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But in Yuhua, we have implemented the PWCS for an existing estate.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will have to phase this out but, currently, the plan is for the new HDB estates.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I will have to check if we, indeed, do have this.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I know that we have enforcement officers there to check for smoky vehicles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, I suppose our enforcement officers can also check for noise pollution.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied): Thank
text: Just two quick questions for the Minister pertaining to the handout under Water Efficiency and Conservation.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied): Thank
text: Can I ask the Minister to give us more details on the community project to replace the nine-litre water closets in low-income households?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied): Thank
text: The second question pertains to the Senior Minister of State Desmond Lee mentioning that 70,000 flats are still eligible for HIP, in MND's COS yesterday.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied): Thank
text: HIP involves the renovation of toilets, spalling concrete and so forth.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied): Thank
text: Would the Ministry consider bringing forward the installation of some of the smart shower devices and these water-efficient water closets under the HIP umbrella, because that may accelerate the Ministry's water conservancy efforts?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, we have decided to do this in new homes because then there is no need for fixtures to be put on by the residents themselves, it can be done by the contractors; study them and, hopefully, it will encourage and motivate them to save water.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Just a quick clarification for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: With regard to waste collection, the PWCS is a very good system.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: I was just wondering about the existing households and estates now and the state of all the bin centres.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Are there measures that we can do to improve the situation for the existing households?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, really, we can only do so much, and education and outreach must go hand in hand.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is key for the National Recycling Programme, where there are recycling bins at every HDB block, one of the issues, of course, is contamination.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We need to continually go out, do outreach, put up signages about proper recycling habits as well as to educate residents on proper recycling habits.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Even with the dual-chute system, we will still need to reach out and educate residents as to how they use these chutes properly.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That experience is the same even in the private residential developments.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We need to go out and reach out.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I want to encourage all Members in this House to work together with us, rally our grassroots and volunteers to reach out regarding, not just imbuing proper recycling habits, but socially-gracious behaviour like not littering, for instance.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Looking at the handout for the Vehicular Emissions Scheme (VES) that will replace the Carbon Emissions-Based Vehicle Scheme (CEVS), it looks like we are reducing the rebate from $30,000 to $20,000 and also reducing the surcharge from the current $30,000 to $20,000.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can the Minister clarify this because it looks like we are taking a step back?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Second, can the Minister clarify if the Government will look into procuring only sustainable palm oil?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The VES first takes into consideration what we think will be the choices made by consumers.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We hope that, at the end of the day, it is either revenue-neutral, at the very least, and that consumers, with this VES incentive or disincentive, will make the right choice.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For the second question, there is already labelling by the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) which encourages big sellers and buyers to comply with sustainable palm oil production.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Most buyers and sellers are in this consortium to make sure they comply.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I think this is currently the best one we have.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To make sure that everybody or compel them to buy only RSPO label products would not be productive nor possible.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I just wanted to make a further clarification about the PWCS.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But that does not preclude anybody else with less than 500 units to put in a PWCS system if they wish.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, there are already private residential developments with less than 500 dwelling units where they have already implemented PWCS.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When I talked about HDB dwelling units, what I am saying is that HDB has announced that they will be implementing PWCS in some of the new estates.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Of course, they have done one at Yuhua, which is an existing estate.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It will depend on HDB's plans, going forward, where else they will be implementing the PWCS system.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.28 pm until 4.50 pm.
